findings.title: Improper iss claim validation accepts an array of issuers (issuer spoofing bypass)
findings.evidence: createVerifier registers the iss validator at line 475 without array:true (contrast aud at line 471), so iss is configured as a scalar StringOrURI claim. The check that should enforce this, validateClaimType (lines 144-152), only verifies each element's primitive type (line 149) and never rejects an array for a non-array claim: the 'array' flag is used solely to choose the error message, and the guard added upstream in 5.0.6/6.0.0 (if (isArray && !allowArray) throw) is absent. verifyToken therefore unwraps the attacker-controlled value at lines 210-212 (arrayValue = Array.isArray(value); values = arrayValue ? value : [value]) and passes the whole array to validateClaimValues, whose check at line 159 (values.some(v => allowed.some(a => a.test(v)))) succeeds if ANY element matches an allowed issuer. Reachability: an attacker who can obtain or influence a signed token whose iss is an array (e.g. a create-token/JWKS endpoint that signs request-controlled claims, a legitimately trusted issuer, or any issuer for which the verifier resolves a trusted key) submits 'iss': ['https://attacker-domain/','https://valid-iss']; with allowedIss:'https://valid-iss' the verifier accepts the token, bypassing issuer pinning, and downstream logic trusting iss (plus libraries such as get-jwks that do not independently validate iss) treats the attacker's token as issued by the trusted issuer. Precondition: the signature must still verify against a key the verifier trusts. Fixed in fast-jwt 5.0.6 (CVE-2025-30144 / GHSA-gm45-q3v2-6cf8) by requiring iss to be a string.
